A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 2 – Teacher’s Notes

Description

In this activity students focus on key vocabulary in questions and scan the texts to find the answer.
They then read in more detail before making their final decision. They are given the rest of the sample
task from the exam to complete within a set time.

Time required:  25 minutes

Materials        A2 Key Handbook (or sample paper)
required:        Student handout 1 and 2
                 Follow-up activity Student handout3(optional)

Aims:            to familiarise students with A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and Writing Part 2
                 to practise scanning for key vocabulary
                 to practise reading for detailed information

Procedure

    1. Explain to your students that they will be doing Part 2 of the A2 Key Paper 1 Reading and
         Writing exam.

    2. Write on the board the following questions.
               What is a blog?
               What do people write about in blogs?
               Have you ever read a blog?
               Have you ever written a blog?

        Ask your students to work in pairs to discuss the questions, elicit their answers and discuss in
        open class.

    3. Explain to your students that they are going to read about 3 people who all write blogs. Ask
         them to read all 3 texts. Students should first identify what each blog is about and then decide
         whose blog they would like to read and why. Set a time limit of 10 minutes and encourage
         students to highlight key words. Encourage students to discuss their favourite blog with their
         partner before getting feedback in open class. Invite students to explain why they prefer one
         blog over another. Take a class vote on the one they like best.

4. Tell your students that they are now going to read for more information. On the board write the
    following question: ‘Who writes both a magazine and a blog?’ Ask your students to underline any
    sentence with ‘magazine’ and ‘blog’ in it for each person, and to check what they learn about
    what each person writes (answer: C, Chrissie).

5. Write the following question on the board ‘Who says that studying and writing a blog at the
    same time can be hard?’. Ask your students if there are different words they could use to
    describe something that is hard e.g. hard = difficult/not easy. Ask students to think about the
    different institutions where students can study e.g. at school/college/university. Ask your
    students to read the text to find the answer to the question. Encourage students to underline the
    words that helped them find the answer. Invite students to compare with their partner and
    explain how they found their answer before open class feedback (answer: B, Dani).

6. Tell your students that they are going to answer questions 9–13 from the sample test. Set them
    a time limit of 7 minutes. This is an individual task. Remind them to use the techniques of
    highlighting key words in the text and thinking about synonyms.

7. Allow your students to check their answers in pairs before open class feedback so again you can
    monitor and hear if they had any problems with the vocabulary.

Suggested follow-up activities
1. Ask students to write their own blog on a topic that interests them.
2. Practise using the answer sheet.Photocopy it and ask students to fill in the lozenges in pencil

     for their answers to Part 2.
